judged_text: uniqueGuests filters guests only against existing attendees and the blacklist, never against duplicates within the guests array, and the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refine that the dialog's hand-copied client schema enforces. A direct addGuests mutation submitting the same email twice (['a@x.com','a@x.com']) passes server validation and reaches the attendees createMany, which throws an unhandled Prisma P2002 unique-constraint error — the caller gets HTTP 500 instead of the BAD_REQUEST the handler promises for invalid emails.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness, unlike the dialog’s client-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `guestsFullDetails` can contain the same email multiple times and is passed to `attendees.createMany`. The handler does not catch database errors around `prisma.booking.update`, so duplicate inserts can bubble up as an internal error rather than the intended `BAD_REQUEST` for invalid input.
